findings.title: No on-chain bound on tick MAGNITUDE. A forward split or administrative multiplier increase harvests real shares, and the only guard is off-chain crank logic.
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md S6 compute_delta_raw requires only m1 >= m0; S10 harvest requires only m1 > m0. No ceiling on m1/m0. PRD F2 step 4 states splits arrive through this same multiplier channel and are 'recorded and skipped' by the tick-watcher, i.e. off-chain. S17 'Reverse splits get two layers of their own' addresses only m1 < m0.
findings.analysis: A forward split RAISES the multiplier. delta = floor(R*(1 - m0/m1)) then sells real exposure, not a dividend. Token-2022 reverts a delegate transfer whose amount exceeds delegated_amount, so a 2x split (delta = 50% of R) reverts on the 5% allowance. The live exposure window is therefore every non-dividend multiplier increase up to m1/m0 <= 1/0.95 = 1.0526: any bump of 5.26% or less executes in full and sells real shares. Repeated smaller ones drain the allowance cumulatively. Nothing on-chain distinguishes a dividend from an administrative correction. The Phase 4 rehearsal hack (Task 4.3: 'temporarily treat Unknown as Dividend') and DT-3's degraded path both widen this.
findings.impact: Falsifies the Scene 3 trust line and the S17 bound. The honest statement is that the ONLY enforced bound is the delegate cap; everything narrower is off-chain policy.
findings.fix: Two lines in compute_delta_raw: require!(m1 <= m0 * MAX_TICK_RATIO). MAX_TICK_RATIO = 1.02 passes every observed real dividend (AAPLx 0.060%, KOx 0.449%, STRCx ~0.51%) with 4x headroom and rejects every split and administrative jump. Plus one test. Phase 1, today, ~10 minutes.

findings.title: Two unreconciled accrual floors, and the crank-side one silently breaks the E-4 receipt triple on the multi-tick path S17 itself calls normal.
findings.evidence: On-chain floor: ARCHITECTURE.md S11 settle accrues into plan.accrued_usdc and pays only when accrued >= config.payout_floor_usdc. Off-chain floor: PRD F4 step 2 ('if the aggregate is worth less than the payout floor, it waits and accrues to the next tick') and PLAN DT-4 ('raise MIN_SWAP_USD so aggregates accrue further before a swap is attempted').
findings.analysis: They cannot both be operative. If the crank holds below its floor it never swaps, so it never calls settle, so accrued_usdc is always 0 and the on-chain accrual is dead code. If the crank swaps every tick, MIN_SWAP_USD is dead and DT-4's remedy is a no-op. On the crank-holds branch two harvests land before one settle, and S10 unconditionally overwrites plan.pending_m0_bits on the second. The receipt then records (m0 = M1_of_tick1, m1 = M2_of_tick2, delta = tick1+tick2), so floor(R*(1-m0/m1)) recomputes only tick 2 and will not equal delta_raw.
findings.impact: The E-4 fix's stated purpose - S17: 'the receipt triple lets anyone recompute what the payout should have been' - is false on exactly the path S17 names as normal for small holders ('roughly two quarters').
findings.fix: One line in harvest: write pending_m0_bits/pending_tick_ts only when plan.pending_raw == 0, so the receipt records the span (m0_first, m1_last). The span telescopes exactly: R*(1-m0/m1) + R*(m0/m1)*(1-m1/m2) = R*(1-m0/m2). Also state in PRD F4 which floor is operative.

findings.title: DT-10 step 3 is factually false against settle.rs, and the tree leads with tax while ignoring the obvious double-taxation counter.
findings.evidence: PLAN S4 DT-10 step 3: 'you can still reinvest. Point the destination at the same stock and stokss does nothing, which is exactly today's behaviour.' ARCHITECTURE.md S11: destination is an InterfaceAccount<TokenAccount> at plan.destination and the only transfer is transfer_checked on usdc_mint. There is no route-back-into-the-stock path; PayoutMode is Cash | Redirect | Bill and settle only ever moves USDC.
findings.analysis: False on two counts. There is no such destination, and even if there were, stokss would not 'do nothing': it harvests, swaps to USDC paying Jupiter spread, then swaps back. Two spreads and a taxable disposal, strictly worse than leaving it alone. Claiming parity with today's behaviour is falsifiable in thirty seconds. Separately, the tree's entire case is tax and it never answers the first thing anyone who does tax will say: selling the increment is itself a taxable disposal, so stokss turns one tax event into two.
findings.fix: Replace step 3 with the true version: opt out per position by not enrolling, or close_plan + revoke in one transaction, which IS exactly today's behaviour and IS implemented. Add the double-taxation answer: the disposal is at near-zero basis delta because you sell the increment the day you receive it, so the capital gain is ~0, and it produces the cash to pay the income tax already owed.

findings.title: DT-9's opening move is a rationalization, and its only substantive answer depends on a feature that is item 2 on the cut list.
findings.evidence: PLAN S4 DT-9 step 1 quotes the rules and concludes 'the objection is aimed at the brief, not at us'. Step 2, the front door, is PLAN cut-order item 2 and Phase 8 is titled 'FIRST TO CUT'.
findings.analysis: Step 1 tells a judge their objection is really an objection to their own rubric. Judges wrote the rubric; they know what 'pick one wedge' meant, and it did not mean 'one instruction is a product'. It also breaks the tree's own opening instruction not to argue the thing is bigger than it looks. And if Phase 8 is cut as planned, the tree is left with a rationalization and a generic appeal.
findings.fix: Drop step 1. Lead with the cut-proof answer: recurring autonomous per-user execution with on-chain receipts is not a feature, it is a service with a clock. The crank running unattended over a weekend and harvesting a corporate action nobody triggered is the app-ness, it is checkable, and it survives every cut.

amended.C-1: Guard accepted, threshold rejected. The critique set MAX_TICK_RATIO = 1.02 on the claim it 'clears every observed tick by ~4x'. Checked against all 570 recorded Dividend events: 1.02 rejects SIX real dividends, one on a tradeable mint (NVOx +2.541%, 2026-03-28). Largest dividend anywhere is WHGROx +2.926%. Raised to 1.03, which rejects zero of the 570. No protection is lost: the smallest possible forward split is 2:1, a ratio of 2.0, so any cap below 2.0 blocks every split. 1.03 gives full split protection with no false rejections.
